messages:
maria: Heads-up — ACME saw ~2x token billing for a single user session after a stream reconnected to a different routing tier. Filed support ticket; attaching notes.
samir: Ugh. Is this the reconnect -> fallback routing case where prefetched KV/prefix ownership didn't follow?
maria: Looks related but the logs show a short window where both the old and new path created provisional ledger entries. Old path later acked a truncated toolcall; new path confirmed the remainder. Both ended up counted.
leo: Can you paste the minimal trace? wondering if session_id stayed the same or we reissued a new session on handoff.
maria: trace (sanitized):
```
span: stream.open session=acme:U123 offset=0
span: route.switch session=acme:U123 -> pool-cheap (sticky=false)
span: stream.truncation offset=1024 toolcall=tts:play
span: stream.reconnect session=acme:U123 offset=1024 -> pool-cheap-quant
ledger.create provisional session=acme:U123 offset=0 count=1024
ledger.create confirmed session=acme:U123 offset=1024 count=768
```
carmen: So both provisional and confirmed cover overlapping token ranges. Ledger never merged because the provisional entry had different "path_id" and we require identical path to dedupe.
tj: Our assumption was path stability. Sticky routing + graceful handoff failures break that. We need attribution by session+offset, not path.
samir: Proposal: add an internal header / field to the routing API: X-Charge-Affinity that carries the session affinity key. On any ledger write we attempt a merge by (session_affinity, offset_range) before creating a new charge record.
leo: Example header sketch:
```
X-Charge-Affinity: session:acme:U123;handshake:2026-03-20T18:03Z
```
maria: Implementation concerns:
- cross-pool lookup could be expensive (need a quick index)
- must be eventual-consistent: do not block request path
- race conditions: two pools might create provisional entries simultaneously
carmen: For the race we can use a lightweight optimistic merge: write provisional with a short TTL and a GUID; reconciler later merges overlapping ranges with last-write-win for confirmed charges.
tj: Telemetry + console UX must show provisional vs confirmed charges so support can explain spikes. Right now console only shows final ledger rows.
samir: Telemetry events we'd add:
- provisional_token_recorded (session_affinity, offset_start, offset_end, path_id, provisional_id)
- provisional_token_merged (provisional_id, confirmed_id, delta)
- token_confirmed
These should be indexed by session_affinity.
leo: Internal API debate: do we extend the public/internal /inference v2 contract? Or add a sidecar reconciliation service that consumes an event stream? Sidecar is lower-risk for rollout.
maria: Sidecar acknowledges look safer: we emit provisional events today and reconciler merges off-cluster. That avoids changing hot RPC path.
carmen: But sidecar means temporary UI gaps until reconciler runs. Could confuse customers if they see provisional spike in billing UI before merge.
tj: UX idea: in Console show a "provisional tokens" toggle and timeline annotation with hover tooltip: "provisional tokens pending reconciliation". Mark reconciler ETA and provide an action "explain to customer" which surfaces related traces.
samir: Rollout plan suggestion:
1) emit provisional events from runtime (non-blocking) — canary 5% (week 1)
2) deploy reconciler sidecar (read-only mode) and validate merges in staging metrics (week 2)
3) enable auto-merge (week 3) behind feature flag
4) enable console "provisional tokens" view for support (week 4)

maria: Ownership: samir + carmen on implementation, leo on reconciler, tj on console. I'll open the RFC and support ticket update.
dev-billing-bot: [automated] Created issue INF-2147: "session-affinity charge merge reconciler" assigned to @samir, @carmen. Priority: P2.
leo: One more thing — we should add an idempotency key for toolcalls so truncated vs resumed fragments map deterministically. Add `toolcall_fragment_id` in the toolcall envelope.
samir: Good call. That reduces overlap heuristics and helps reconciler. We'll prototype in the canary.
maria: Thanks all. I'll paste RFC link shortly and add sample logs for support to triage.
